I.definition: I i. This letter represents, in Latin, I. The vowel whose short and long sounds are heard in the English word deceit.—II. Before a, e, o, or u in the same syllable, the consonant which begins the English words yam, ye…

Ianiculum.definition: Iāniculum ī, n Ianus, one of the hills of Rome, site of the mythical citadel of Janus, C., L., V., O.

Ianuarius.definition: Iānuārius adj. Ianus, of Janus: mensis, January.—As subst m. (sc. mensis), a. d. VII. Idūs Ianuari, Cs.—Of January, of the month of January: Kalendis Ianuariis, on New-year's day: Nonae, Cs.

Ianus.definition: Iānus ī, m IA-, an old Italian deity, good of doors, passages, and entrances, of all beginnings, and of the month of January: anceps, with two faces, O.: bifrons, V.: Ianus Quirini, H.—The temple of Janus: ad infimum …

Iapys.definition: Iāpys ydis, adj., of the Iapydes (in Illyria), V.

Iapyx.definition: Iāpyx ygis, adj., of Iapyx, Iapygian, Apulian, Calabrian: equus, V.— As subst: Daunus, i. e. king of Apulia, O.; (sc. ventus), the wind from Apulia, V., H.

Ilium1.definition: Īlium or Īlion ī, n (C., V., H., O.), *)/ilion, or Ilios, ī, f (H., O.), *)/ilios, Ilium, Troy.

Indiges1.definition: 'Indiges etis, m indu+GEN-, a deified hero, patron deity (of a country): Indigetem Aeneam . . . Deberi caelo, V.: Indigetes di (old prayer), L.'

Inuus.definition: Inuus ī, m an old name of Lupercus (Pan), L.

Isthmia.definition: Isthmia ōrum, n, ta *)/isthmia, the Isthmian games (every five years near Corinth), L.

Iudaicus.definition: Iūdaicus or Iūdaeicus adj., Jewish: aurum: bellum, Ta.: ius, Iu.: panis, unleavened, Ta.

Iugarius.definition: Iugārius adj., of Iuno Iuga (goddess of marriage): vicus (in which stood her altar), L.

Iuno.definition: Iūnō ōnis, f a daughter of Saturn, sister and wife of Jupiter, goddess of marriage, C., V., H., O.: Iuno Lucina, T.: urbs Iunonis, i. e. Argos, O.— Prov.: Iunonis sacra ferre, i. e. to walk as in solemn procession, H.…

Iunonalis.definition: Iūnōnālis e, adj., of Juno: tempus, i. e. the month of June, O.

Iunonicola.definition: Iūnōnicola ae, m Iuno+COL-, a worshipper of Juno, O.

Iunonigena.definition: Iūnōnigena ae, m Iuno+GEN-, born of Juno, i. e. Vulcan, O.

Iunonius.definition: Iūnōnius adj., of Juno, Junonian, V., O.

iacens.definition: iacēns ntis, adj. P. of iaceo, prostrate, fallen: domus: statuae: hostis, H.—Plur m. as subst, the fallen, dead, Cs.—Fig., cast down, fallen: voltūs, O.: oculos, O.—Of words, at hand, in common use.

iacio.definition: iaciō iēcī, iactus, ere IA-, to throw, cast, fling, hurl: tela, S.: lapides iaciendos curare: in alquem scyphum: in murum lapides, Cs.: pilam ponto, V.: sese Fluctibus mediis, V.: plumbum Funda iacit, O.: ancoris iact…

iactans.definition: iactāns antis, adj. with comp. P. of iacto, boastful, vainglorious: iactantior Ancus, V., H.

iactanter.definition: 'iactanter adv. with comp. iactans, ostentatiously, boastfully: litteras componere, Ta.: iactantius moerere, Ta.'

iactantia.definition: īactantia ae, f iacto, a boasting, display, ostentation: militaris, Ta.: verborum, Ta.

iactatio.definition: iactātiō ōnis, f iacto, a tossing, shaking agitation, motion: corporis, gesticulation: volneris, L.: ex magnā iactatione terram videre.— Fig., agitation: iactationes animorum incitatae: popularis, stirring the populac…

iactatus.definition: iactātus ūs, m iacto, a throwing to and fro, tossing.—Plur.: pennarum, O.

iactito.definition: iactitō —, —, āre, freq. iacto, to make a show of, display: ridicula intexta versibus, L.: officium, Ph.

iacto.definition: iactō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. iacio, to throw, cast, hurl: semina per undas, scatter, O.: hastas: de muro vestem, Cs.: cinerem per agros, V.: Saxa saxis (i. e. in saxa), O.—To throw about, toss about, shake, flourish: d…

iactura.definition: iactūra ae, f IA-, a throwing, throwing away, throwing overboard: in mari facienda equi: naufragium iacturā redimit, Cu.—A sacrifice, outlay, expense, cost: non magnā iacturā factā.—Loss, damage, detriment: vitae, Cs.…

iactus2.definition: iactus ūs, m IA-, a throwing, casting, hurling, throw, cast: fulminum: Pulveris, V.: teli iactu abesse, a spear's throw, L.: femineus, i. e. by a woman, O.: quatere fenestras Iactibus, i. e. by throwing stones, H.—Of …

iaculabilis.definition: iaculābilis e, adj. iaculor, to be hurled, fit for throwing: telum, O.

iaculator.definition: iaculātor ōris, m iaculor, a thrower, caster, hurler: audax (truncorum), H.: maximus, a crack shot, Iu.: Lycotas, the spearman, O.—Plur, lightarmed soldiers, carrying javelins, L.

iaculatrix.definition: iaculātrīx īcis, f iaculator, a javelin thrower, huntress: (Diana), O.

iaculor.definition: iaculor ātus, ārī, dep. iaculum, to throw, cast, hurl: e nubibus ignem, V.: silicem in hostīs, O.: puppibus ignes (i. e. in puppī s), V.—To throw the javelin, fight with the javelin: laudem consequi iaculando: totum d…

iaculum.definition: iaculum ī, n IA-, a dart, javelin: iaculorum multitudo: iacula eminus emissa, S.: (litterae) in iaculo inligatae, Cs.: iaculi certamina, V.: trans finem expeditum, H.—A casting-net, fishing-net, O.

iam1.definition: iam adj. I. Of time, at the moment, at the present moment, now, at this time, just now, at present: iam satis credis sobrium esse me, T.: saltūs reficit iam roscida luna, V.: Iam melior, iam, diva, precor, V.: iura ip…

iam2.definition: iam dūdum, iam iam, iam iamque, iam pridem, iandūdum see iam.

ianitor.definition: īānitor ōris, m ianua, a door-keeper, porter, janitor: carceris: Crispini, H.: Caeli, i. e. Janus, O.: ingens, Cerberus, V.

ianua.definition: iānua ae, f IA-, a door, house-door: nostra, T.: Ciceronis, S.: frangere, H.—An entrance, gate, door: inferni regis, V.: urbs Asiae, the key: gemini vasta maris, O.: Ianua Baiarum est, on the way to, Iu.—Fig., an entr…

ibis.definition: ībis idis (acc. ībim, C., ībin, O., Iu.; plur. ībes, C., acc. ībīs, C.), f, i)=bis, the ibis (a water-bird of Egypt).

ico.definition: (īcō) īcī, īctus, ere (in class. prose only perf. system) 1 IC-, to strike, hit, smite, stab, sting: in proelio telo ictus: lapide ictus, Cs.: in turbā ictus cecidit, L.: icta securibus ilex, V.: vix icto aë re, hardl…

ictus2.definition: īctus ūs, m 1 IC-, a blow, stroke, stab, cut, thrust, bite, sting, wound: uno ictu securis: gladiatoris: scutis uno ictu pilorum transfixis, Cs.: non caecis ictibus volnerari, L.: medicari cuspidis ictum, V.: arboris,…

iecusculum.definition: iecusculum ī, n dim. iecur, a little liver.

ieiune.definition: iēiūnē adj. with comp. ieiunus, meagrely, dryly, feebly, without ornament, spiritlessly: disputare: dici ieiunius.

ieiunitas.definition: iēiūnitās ātis, f ieiunus.—Prop., a fasting; hence, fig., of speech, dryness, poverty, meagreness: ieiunitatem et famem malle quam, etc.: bonarum artium, destitution.

ieiunium.definition: iēiūnium ī, n ieiunus, a fasting, fast-day, fast: instituendum Cereri, L.: longa ieiunia, O.: ieiunia indicere, H.—Hunger: ieiunia pascere, O —Leanness, poorness (of animals), V.

ieiunus.definition: iēiūnus adj. with comp, fasting, abstinent, hungry: plebecula: canis, H.: serpens, Pr.: cor pora, L.: lupus ieiunis dentibus acer, H.: fames, extreme, Iu.: odium, i. e. on an empty stomach, Iu.: ieiunae negare aquam, …

ignave.definition: īgnāvē adv. with comp. ignavus, sluggishly, slothfully, without spirit: ne quid faciamus: dicere multa, flatly, H.: carpere ignavius herbas, V.

ignigena.definition: īgnigena ae, m ignis+GEN-, the fire-born, son of fire (of Bacchus), O.

ignipes.definition: īgnipēs pedis, adj. ignis+pes, fiery-footed, O.

ignipotens.definition: īgnipotēns entis, adj. ignis+potens, potent in fire, ruler of fire: deus (Vulcan), V.

ignorans.definition: īgnōrāns antis, adj. P. of ignoro, not knowing, ignorant: Fovit volnus lymphā Ignorans, without knowing its power, V.: eventū s belli, Cs.

ignoratus.definition: īgnōrātus adj. P. of ignoro, undetected, unperceived: Romanos adgreditur, S.—Involuniary (opp. voluntarius).

ignoscens.definition: (īgnōscēns, entis) adj. P. of ignosco.—Only comp, forgiving, placable: animus ignoscentior, T.

ignotus2.definition: īgnōtus adj. with comp. and sup. in+ (g)notus, unknown, strange, unrecognized, unfamiliar: locus, T.: ignotior gens, L.: adversus ignotos inter se, L.: bella, of uncertain result, V.: favos ignotus adedit Stellio, unn…

illa.definition: illā adv. abl f. of ille, sc. viā, in that way, in that direction, there: Oceanum illā tentavimus, Ta.: revertebar illā, quā, etc., O.

illa-.definition: illa- in compounds with in; see inla-.

illac.definition: illāc adv. abl f. of illic, sc. viā, that way, on that side, there: hac atque illac perfluo, T.: omnīs illac facere, belong to that party: nunc hac . . . nunc illac, on one side . . . on the other, O.

ille-.definition: ille- in words compounded with in; see inle-.

illi.definition: illī adv. old locat. of ille, there, therein: Nam illi haud licebat loqui, etc., T.: praeclara illi laudatur hiaspis, Iu.—Fig., in that affair: ego illi maxumam partem feram, T.

illic2.definition: illīc adv. illi+ce, in that place, yonder, there: melius, hic quae fiunt, quam illic, scio, T.: plurīs illic offendisse inimicos, quam hic reliquisse: Utque aër, tellus illic, O.: illic, ubi nulla incendia, Iu.: qui i…

illim.definition: illim adv. ille, from that place, thence: me illim abstraxi, T.: amorem abiecisse illim, i. e. from her.—Of time, thenceforth: usque ad nostram memoriam, S.

illo.definition: illō adv. ille, to that place, thither: advenio, T.: adit, Cs.: accedere.

illoc.definition: illōc adv. old for illuc, thither, T.

illuc.definition: illūc adv. illic, to that place, thither: huc vel illuc inpelli, T.: huc illuc agitare, S.: huc atque illuc intuens: huc et illuc cursitant, H.: illuc ex his vinculis, i. e. into the other world: illuc Ire, ubi, etc.,…

imaginor.definition: imāginor ātus, ārī, dep. imago, to picture to oneself, fancy: pavorem eorum, Ta.

imbecille.definition: (imbēcillē) adv. imbecillus, weakly, feebly. —Only comp: imbecillius adsentiri, with hesitation.

imberbis.definition: 'imberbis (inb-) e, adj. 2 in+barba, without a beard, beardless: pater: quae Imberbes didicere, H.'

imitatus.definition: imitātus adj. P. of imitor, fictitious: sim<*> lacra: voluptas, O.

imitor.definition: imitor ātus, āre, freq. 2 IC-, to imitate, act like, copy after, seek to resemble, counterfeit, mimic: genus ad omnia imitanda aptissimum, Cs.: in gloriā Paulum: aliquem imitando effingere: imitari quam invidere bonis…

immane.definition: immāne (inm-) adv. immanis, frightfully, fiercely, savagely: leo hians, V.: sonat fluctus, V.

immensum1.definition: immēnsum (inm-) ī, n immensus, a boundless extent, vastness, immensity: per immensum actus, O.: mons in immensum editus, S.: ad immensum multitudinis speciem augere, L.

immensum2.definition: immēnsum (inm-) adv. immensus, without end, exceedingly, immensely: creverat, O.

immerito.definition: immeritō (inm-) adv. with sup. immeritus, undeservedly, unjustly, without cause: accusare me inmeritissumo, T.: si immerito, si misera, etc.

immisericorditer.definition: 'immisericorditer adv. immisericors, unmercifully: factum a vobis, T.'

immoderate.definition: immoderātē (inm-) adv. with comp. immoderatus, without measure, by no rule: vox profusa.—Fig., immoderately, extravagantly: vivere: abuti nostrā facilitate: ferre immoderatius casum.

immodeste.definition: immodestē adv. immodestus, immoderately, shamelessly: gloriari, L.

immodice.definition: immodicē adv. immodicus, beyond measure, excessively: gloriari, L.: potestate uti, L.

immordeo.definition: (immordeō or in-m-) —, sus, ēre, to bite into.—Only P. pass.: immorso collo, Pr.: stomachus pernā immorsus, i. e. stimulated, H.

impastus.definition: impāstus (in-p-) adj., unfed, hungry: leo, V.

impatienter.definition: 'impatienter (in-p-) adv. with comp, with impatience: indoluit, Ta.: captivitatem impatientius timere, Ta.'

impavide.definition: impavidē adv. impavidus, fearlessly, intrepidly: exhausto poculo, L.

impeditus.definition: impedītus (inp-) adj. with comp. and sup. P. of impedio, hindered, embarrassed, obstructed, encumbered, burdened, impeded: impeditis hostibus propter onera, Cs.: comitatus: agmen, L.: magnam partem eorum impeditam int…

impendio.definition: impendiō (inp-) adv. abl. of impendium, by a great deal, very much: magis, far more, T., C.

imperans.definition: imperāns (inp-) ntis, m P. of impero, a master, conqueror, ruler.

imperatum.definition: imperātum ī, n P. of impero, a command, order: imperatum facit, obeys, Cs.: imperata facere, Cs.: ad imperatum non venire, according to orders, Cs.

imperite.definition: imperītē adv. with comp. and sup. imperitus, unskilfully, ignorantly, awkwardly: facit: quid potuit dici imperitius?: imperitissime dictum.

imperiuratus.definition: imperiūrātus (in-p-) adj., by which no false oath is taken: aquae (of the Styx), O.

impertior.definition: impertior —, —, īrī, dep. collat. form of impertio, to take as a partner, make a sharer in: eram hoc malo, T.

impertita.definition: impertīta ōrum, n P. of impertio, favors, concessions: pro his impertitis, L.

impes.definition: '(impes or inpes, petis) m in+PET-, violence, vehemence, force (only abl sing.): impete vasto ferri, O.: certo impete, O.'

impetrio.definition: impetriō —, —, īre, desid. impetro, to seek through omens, inquire for by auspices: avibus res impetriri solebant: qui impetrire velit.

impie.definition: impiē (inp-) adv. impius, irreligiously, undutifully: in nos facere: deserere regem, Cu.

impigre.definition: impigrē adv. impiger, actively, quickly, readily: hostium res attendere, S.: consulem sequi, L.

implacabiliter.definition: (implācābiliter) adv., implacably.—Only comp: implacabilius irasci, Ta.

implexus.definition: implexus P. in+plexus, interwoven, entwined: implexae crinibus anguī s Eumenides, V. —Involved: luctu continuo, Ta.

implicatus.definition: implicātus (inpl-) adj. P. of implico, entangled, involved, confused: nec in sermone quicquam: partes orationis.

importune.definition: importūnē (inp-) adv. importunus, unsuitably, rudely, violently: insistere.

impotenter.definition: (impotenter) adv. impotens, weakly, ineffectually.—Only comp: impotentius regi, L.

impressus2.definition: 'impressus (in-pr-) adj., unpressed, not milked: ubera, Pr.'

improbe.definition: improbē (inp-) adv. with comp. and sup. improbus, badly, wrongly, wickedly, recklessly: multa fecisti: dici: improbius fieri: quas (res) improbissime fecit: decerpere oscula, Ct.

improperatus.definition: improperātus (in-pr-) adj., not hasty, lingering: vestigia, V.

improsper.definition: imprōsper (in-p-) era, erum, adj., unfortunate, unprosperous: fortuna, Ta.: Claritudo generis, Ta.

improviso.definition: imprōvīsō (in-p-) adv. improvisus, on a sudden, unexpectedly: pagum adoriri, Cs.: ut tempestates improviso concitantur: apparuit ignis, V.: repertus, O.

improvisus.definition: imprōvīsus (in-pr-) adj. with comp, not foreseen, unforeseen, unexpected: malum, S.: sapienti nihil improvisum accidere potest: pupilli calamitas: adventus: vis leti, H.: Improvisi aderunt, V.: anguis, concealed, V.: …

imprudenter.definition: imprūdenter (inpr-) adv. with comp. imprudens, without foresight, ignorantly, inconsiderately: putant: facere, N.: accessit imprudentius, T.

impudenter.definition: 'impudenter (inp-) adv. with comp. and sup. impudens, shamelessly, impudently: facere, T.: loqui: impudentius ab sociis abstulit: impudentissime mentiri.'

impulsus2.definition: impulsus (inp-) ūs, m 1 in+1 PAL-, a striking against, push, pressure, shock, impulse: impulsu scutorum copiae pulsae: alieno impulsu moveri: dimotis inpulsu pectoris undis, O.—Fig., incitement, instigation, influence…

impune.definition: impūne (inp-) adv. with comp. impunis, without punishment, unpunished, with impunity: haec facere, T.: facere (iniuriam) impune si possis: iniurias tulisse, inflicted, Cs.: occidi, unavenged: iniuriam accepisse, S.: a…

impunite.definition: impūnītē adv. impunitus, with impunity: facere.

impunitus.definition: impūnītus (in-p-) adj. with comp, unpunished, unrestrained, free from danger, safe, secure: iniuria: scelus, S.: nec diu proditoribus impunita res fuit, L.: qui tu impunitior illa obsonia captas? H.: quo inpunitior si…

impuratus.definition: impūrātus (inp-) adj. impurus, defiled, infamous, abandoned, vile: ille, that vile wretch, T.: hunc inpuratum Ulcisci, T.

impure.definition: impūrē adv. with sup. impurus, basely, shamefully, vilely, infamously: impure atque flagitiose vivere: a quo impurissime haec nostra fortuna despecta est.

imputatus2.definition: imputātus (inp-) adj. 2 in+putatus, unpruned, untrimmed: vinea, H.

in-.definition: in- an inseparable particle cf. Gr. a)-, a)n-; Germ. and Eng. un-, which, prefixed to an adj., negatives or reverses the meaning: impar, unequal: intolerabilis, unbearable: immitis, ruthless. —In tmesis: Hanc . . . In…

inaequaliter.definition: inaequāliter adv. inaequalis, unequally, disproportionately: deprimere alios, alios extollere, L.: campus sinuatur, Ta.

inaniter.definition: ināniter adv. inanis, vainly, idly, uselessly: exsultare: pectus angere, H.

inaratus.definition: in-arātus adj., unploughed, untilled, fallow: terra, V.: tellus, H.

inardesco.definition: in-ārdēscō ārsī, —, ere, inch, to kindle, take fire, burn, glow: nubes Solis inardescit radiis, V.: aestuosius, H.— Fig.: amor specie praesentis inarsit, O.: cupidine vindictae, Ta.

inauditus.definition: in-audītus adj., unheard-of, unusual, strange, new, incredible: agger novi generis atque inauditus, Cs.: scelus: incredibilis atque inaudita gravitas: cui sunt inauditae querellae tuae?: volucres, Ta.—Unheard, not bro…

inaugurato.definition: inaugurātō adv. (P. of inauguro, abl absol.), after taking auguries, with regard to omens: id inaugurato facere, L.: consecrare locum, L.

inauratus.definition: inaurātus adj. P. of inauro, gilded, golden: statua: quem inauratum in Capitolio fuisse, etc. (i. e. cuius statuam): acanthus, O.: Hercules, Iu.

inauspicatus.definition: in-auspicātus adj., without consulting the auspices: lex, passed without omens, L.

incallide.definition: incallidē adv. incallidus, unskilfully: non incallide, cleverly.

incanesco.definition: (in-cānēscō) canuī, —, ere, inch, to become white, turn gray, grow hoary (only perf.): ornusque incanuit albo Flore piri, V.

incassum.definition: 'in-cassum or in cassum adv. see cassus, in vain, to no purpose, uselessly: furere, V.: tot pati labores, V.: missae preces, L.: studio gestire lavandi, wantonly, V.'

incaute.definition: incautē adv. with comp. incautus, incautiously, inconsiderately, recklessly: stulte omnia et incaute: pugnare, L.: incautius custodiae dispositae, Cs.: murum incautius subit, L.

incensus1.definition: incēnsus adj. P. of incendo, inflamed, fiery, hot: incensos aestū s avertere, V.: in meditando.

incensus2.definition: incēnsus adj. 2 in+census, not assessed, unregistered: hominem incensum vendere: populus, L.—Plur m. as subst: lex de incensis lata, L.

inceptor.definition: inceptor ōris, m 1 in+CAP-, a beginner: mearum voluptatum, T.

inceptum.definition: inceptum ī, n P. neut. of incipio, a beginning: incepta gravia, H.— An attempt, undertaking: illud, T.: contra patriam: a quo incepto me detinere, S.: cuius neque inceptum ullum frustra erat, S.: absistere incepto, L.…

inceptus2.definition: (inceptus, ūs) m 1 in+CAP-, a beginning, undertaking (only abl sing.): turpe inceptūst, T.: foedum inceptu, foedum exitu, L.

incertum1.definition: incertum ī, n incertus, an uncertainty: ne cuius incerti vanique auctor esset, L.: scribere legiones ad incerta belli, contingencies, L.: Haud incerta cano, V.: bona omnium in dubium incertumque revocabuntur: praefect…

incertum2.definition: 'incertum adv. neut. of incertus, doubtfully: vigilans, half awake, O.'

inceste.definition: incestē adv. incestus, impurely, with pollution: facere sacrificium Dianae, L.: eā (aquā) uti.

incestum.definition: incestum ī, n 1 incestus, impious unchastity, incest: incestum supremo supplicio sancire: facere: ab incesto id ei loco nomen factum, L.— Plur., C.

incestus1.definition: incestus adj. 2 in+castus, not religiously pure, unclean, impure, polluted, defiled, sinful, criminal: virum incesto ore lacerare: incesto addidit integrum, punished the good with the bad, H.: an triste bidental Mover…

incestus2.definition: (incestus, ūs) m 2 in+2 CAD-, unchastity, incest.—Only abl: quaestio de incestu.

inchoo2.definition: inchoō āvī, ātus, āre, to begin, commence: signum ab alio incohatum absolvere: initium sedis ab saltu, Ta.: Stygio regi aras, i. e. begins to sacrifice, V.: spem longam, entertain, H.—Of a writer or speaker, to essay …

incido1.definition: incidō cidī, —, ere 1 in+cado, to fall in, fall, light, strike, reach, find the way: umeri surgunt quā tegmina summa, incidit (hasta), V.: Incidit spatium rhombi Implevitque sinūs, i. e. happens into a net, Iu.: in fo…

incido2.definition: incīdō cīdī, cīsus, ere 1 in+caedo, to cut into, cut through, cut open, cut away: venas hominis: teneris arboribus incisis, Cs.: pinnas, clip: vites falce, V.: pulmo incisus, divided: linum, sever.—To cut upon, carve,…

incise.definition: incīsē adv. incisus, in short clauses: dicere.

incisum.definition: incīsum ī, n incisus, a section, division, clause (in a period): quae.

incitate.definition: (incitātē) adv. incitatus.—Only comp., of speech, vehemently, rapidly: fluit incitatius.

incitatus.definition: incitātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of incito, hurried, rapid, swift, at full speed: equo incitato se in hostes immittens: cursu incitato, Cs.: mundi incitatissima conversio.—Fig., vehement, ardent, rapid: cursus in…

inclementer.definition: inclēmenter adv. with comp. inclemens, rigorously, harshly, roughly, severely: increpantes, L.: dictum in se inclementius, T.: inclementius in te invehi, L.

inclinatus.definition: inclīnātus adj. with comp. P. of inclino, inclined, disposed, prone: plebs inclinatior ad Poenos, L.: animus ad pacem inclinatior, L.: inclinatis ad suspicionem mentibus, Ta.—Depressed, sunken: vox, low.—Fig., sunken,…

incogitans.definition: in-cōgitāns antis, adj., thoughtless, inconsiderate: ni fuissem incogitans, T.

incohatus.definition: incohātus adj. P. of incoho, begun, unfinished, incomplete, imperfect: Veneris partem, quam Apelles incohatam reliquisset, absolvere: rem tam praeclaram incohatam relinquere.

incomitatus.definition: in-comitātus adj., unaccompanied, unattended, alone: Andromache, V.: virtus incomitata bonis, O.

incommode.definition: incommodē adv. with comp. and sup. incommodus, inconveniently, unsuitably, unfortunately, unseasonably: venire: accidit, Cs.: adversari, L.: cum illo actum optime est, mecum incommodius: incommodissime navigare.

incommodum.definition: incommodum ī, n incommodus, inconvenience, trouble, disadvantage, detriment, injury, misfortune, loss: ex incommodis Alterius sua ut conparent commoda, T.: incommodi nihil capere: ex his incommodis pecuniā se liberare…

incomposite.definition: incompositē adv. incompositus, without order, disorderly: veniens, L.: fugere, Cu.

incomptus.definition: in-cōmptus (incōmt-) adj., disordered, dishevelled, unkempt, unadorned: capilli, H.: caput, H.: nuda, nudis incompta capillis, O.: apparatū s, Ta.—Fig., of speech, artless, rude, unadorned: oratio: ars: (versū s), V., H.

incondite.definition: inconditē adv. inconditus, confusedly, without order: incondite fundit quantum potest.

inconsiderate.definition: incōnsīderātē adv. inconsideratus, inconsiderately, rashly: agere: dicere.

inconstans.definition: in-cōnstāns antis, adj. with comp, changeable, fickle, capricious, inconsistent: ridicule: quid inconstantius Deo?: litterae.

inconsulte.definition: incōnsultē adv. with comp. inconsultus, unadvisedly, inconsiderately: dicere: commissum proelium, L.: inconsultius procedere, Cs.: paulo inconsultius adgredi, S.

incorrupte.definition: incorruptē adv. with comp. incorruptus, uncorruptly, justly: iudicare: incorruptius iudicare.

increbresco.definition: in-crēbrēscō (-bēscō) bruī, —, ere, to quicken, grow, increase, rise, spread: ventus: auster increbruit, Cs.: increbrescente vento, rising, L.: nemorum murmur, V.: si increbruit aura, H.: numerus: rem ad triarios redi…

incredibiliter.definition: incrēdibiliter adv. incredibilis, incredibly, extraordinarily: delector: pertimuit.

incresco.definition: in-crēscō ēvī, —, ere, to grow upon: cuti squamas increscere, O.: saxum increscere ligno, grow over (i. e. encroach upon), O.— To grow, swell, be swollen: lacrimis quoque flumina dicunt Increvisse suis, O.— To grow in…

incruentatus.definition: in-cruentātus adj., not made bloody, unwounded: Inque cruentatus Caeneus, O.

inculte.definition: incultē adv. with comp, without refinement, coarsely: vivere: incultius agitare, S.—Of speech, roughly, rudely: dicere.

incultus1.definition: in-cultus adj. with comp, untilled, uncultivated: ager: solum: loca, S.— Plur n. as subst: culta ab incultis notare, L.—Wild, uncultivated: sentes, V.—Neglected, unpeopled, abandoned: via: quid incultius oppidis?—Undr…

incultus2.definition: in-cultus ūs, m want of cultivation, neglect: incultu foeda eius (loci) facies, S.: honores desertos per incultum, L.

incuriose.definition: incūriōsē adv. with comp. incuriosus, carelessly, negligently: castra posita, L.: incuriosius agere, Ta.

incurvatus.definition: incurvātus adj. P. of incurvo, bent, crooked, bowed: bacillum: membra dolore, O.

incussus2.definition: (incussus, ūs) m incutio, a shock, dashing against (only abl sing.): armorum, Ta.

indago1.definition: indāgō āvī, ātus, āre indu+1 AG-, to trace out, track: canis natus ad indagandum.— Fig., to investigate, explore, hunt for, trail: quod in causā quaerendum est: indicia exiti: de re p.

indago2.definition: indāgō inis, f indu+1 AG-, an encircling with toils, surrounding: saltūs indagine cingunt, V.: indaginis modo silvas persultare, Ta.: velut indagine Samnites agere, hunt like game, L.

inde.definition: inde adv.—Of place, from that place, thence: si te inde exemerim (i. e. ex pistrino), T.: mansi Calibus, inde has litteras dedi: in provinciam exire, atque inde contendere, Cs.: haud procul inde ubi est, etc., L.: ses…

indecore.definition: indecōrē adv. indecorus, unbecomingly, indecently: facere: haud indecore, Ta.

indeiectus.definition: in-dēiectus adj., not thrown down: domus, O.

index.definition: index dicis, m and f in+DIC-, one who points out, a discloser, discoverer, informer, witness: falsus, S.: haec omnia indices detulerunt.— An informer, betrayer, spy: vallatus indicibus: saeptus armatis indicibus: sile…

indicens.definition: in-dīcēns entis, adj., that does not say: Non me indicente haec fiunt, not without my telling, T.: me indicente, L.

indico1.definition: indicō āvī, ātus, āre index, to point out, indicate, inform, show, declare, disclose, make known, reveal, betray: de coniuratione, S.: causam pestis, L.: indicatis deprehensisque internuntiis, Cs.: aliquid in volgus, …

indico2.definition: in-dīcō dīxī, dictus, ere, to declare publicly, proclaim, publish, announce, appoint: concilium in diem certam, Cs.: forum, V.: ieiunia, H.: dies indicta pugnae, L.: funus ut indicatur, that invitations be issued: div…

indictus2.definition: in-dictus adj., not said, unsaid: Quod dic tum, indictumst, T.: ea ut indicta sint, revocare L.: carminibus nostris indictus, unsung, V.: in signe, adhuc Indictum ore alio, H.: indictā causā interfecti, without a hear…

indigens.definition: indigēns ntis, adj. P. of indigeo, in want of, needing: mei: alienarum opum, N.—Plur. as subst: indigentibus benigne facere, the poor.

indiges2.definition: indigēs is, adj. indu+EG-, needy, indigent, Pac. ap. C.

indignandus.definition: indīgnandus adj. P. of indignor, to be despised, deserving contempt: (vestis) lecto, O.

indignans.definition: indīgnāns antis, adj. P. of indignor, impatient, reluctant, indignant: venti, V.: ursi, O.

indignatus.definition: indīgnātus adj. P. of indignor, angered, reluctant: Vita fugit sub umbras, V.

indigne.definition: indīgnē adv. with comp. and sup. indignus, unworthily, undeservedly, dishonorably, shamefully: Facis iniuriam illi, T.: indignius obtrectatum esse, ne, etc.: indignissime interire, Cs.—Angrily, indignantly: neque indi…

indiligens.definition: in-dīligēns tis, adj. with comp, careless, heedless, negligent: nimium, T.: pater familias, N.: si indiligentiores fuerint, Cs.

inditus.definition: 'inditus adj. P. of indo, put on, laid on, imposed. vincula, Ta.: custodes, Ta.'

individuum.definition: indīviduum ī, n individuus, an atom, indivisible particle.

indocte.definition: in-doctē adv. indoctus, unlearnedly, unskilfully: facere.

indu.definition: indu old for 1 in; see indipiscor, indoles, induperator, industrius, indutiae.

indulgens.definition: indulgēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of indulgeo, indulgent, kind, tender, fond: nomen indulgentius maternum: ministri irarum, L.: obsequium peccatis indulgens: sibi hydrops, H.: civitas in captivos, L.

induperator.definition: induperātor ōris, m indupero, old for impero, a commander-in-chief, emperor: barbarus, Iu.

induratus.definition: indūrātus adj. P. of induro, hardened.— Fig.: induratus resistendo hostium timor, L.

indutus2.definition: (indūtus ūs), m a putting on.—Only dat: quam (vestem) indutui gerebat, Ta.

inelegans.definition: in-ēlegāns antis, adj., not choice, inelegant: orationis copia.

inepte.definition: ineptē adv. ineptus, improperly, impertinently, absurdly: disserere: dicere: nil molitur inepte, H.: fautor (i. e. favens), H.

inerrans.definition: in-errāns tis, adj., not wandering, fixed: stellae.

inexpeditus.definition: (in-expedītus) adj., not free, entangled, confused.—Only comp: pugna inexpeditior, L.

inexplorato.definition: inexplōrātō adv. abl. of inexploratus, without previous examination: profectus, L.: angustiis superatis, L.

infacetiae.definition: īnfacētiae (infic-) ārum, f coarse jokes, tasteless attempts at wit, Ct.

infamatus.definition: īnfamātus adj. P. of infamo, of ill repute: dea, O.

infans.definition: īnfāns fantis, adj. with comp. and sup. 2 in + for, that cannot speak, without speech, mute, speechless: statuae, H.: filium, cum infans esset, locutum.—Poor of speech, not eloquent: homines: pudor, i. e. embarrassmen…

infectus1.definition: īnfectus adj. 2 in+factus, not done, unwrought, unmade, undone, unaccomplished, unfinished: pro infecto haberi: omnia pro infecto sint, be regarded, L.: infectum reddet quod, etc., undo, H.: infectā pace dimissi, with…

infeliciter.definition: īnfēlīciter adv. infelix, unhappily, unfortunately: fit mihi obviam, T.: tentata res, L.

infense.definition: (īnfēnsē) adv. infensus, with hostility, bitterly: invectus, Ta.: Isocrati adversatus infensius: infensius pugnare, L.

infercio.definition: īnferciō —, —, īre 1 in+farcio, to stuff in, force in: inferciens verba.

inferior.definition: īnferior ius, adj. comp. of inferus, lower, further down: spatium, Cs.: locus (opp. superior): in inferius ferri, downwards, O.: Africae pars, i. e. nearer the sea, S.: caelum sidet inferius mari, H.: effigies, smalle…

infeste.definition: īnfēstē adv. with comp. and sup. infestus, inimically, violently, outrageously: quae in nos fecerint, L.: infestius circumscindere, L.: infestissime contendere.

infideliter.definition: īnfidēliter adv., faithlessly, perfidiously: nec aliquid senatui suadere.

infinite.definition: īnfīnītē adv. infinitus, without bounds, without end, infinitely: ne infinite feratur ut flumen oratio: quod faciendum est in perorando, without restraint.—Without exception, universally: res infinite posita.

infirme.definition: īnfīrmē adv. infirmus, faintly, slightly: animatus.

infit.definition: īn-fit defect, begins: ita farier, V.—Begins to speak; his vocibus infit, V.: ita Tullus infit: Romani, etc., L.: ibi infit, se agere, etc., L.: causam scitantibus infit, O.

infitiae.definition: (īnfitiae, ārum) f 2 in+1 FA-, denial.— Only acc., in the phrase, infitias ire, to deny: quod nemo it infitias, N.: neque infitias eo, nos dedisse, etc., L.: ille infitias ibit, T.: infitias eunt mercedem se pactos, L.

inflate.definition: (īnflātē) adv. 1 inflatus.—Only comp, haughtily, proudly, pompously: inflatius commemorare, Cs.: haec perscribebat, with exaggeration, Cs.

inflatus1.definition: īnflātus adj. with comp. P. of inflo, swelled up, swollen, puffed up: serpens inflato collo: amnes, L.—Fig., puffed up, inflated, haughty, proud: animus: regis pollicitationibus, Cs.: promissis: iactatione, L.: his op…

inflatus2.definition: īnflātus ūs, m inflo, a blowing in, blast: (tibiae) si inflatum non recipiunt: primo inflatu tibicinis.—Fig., a breathing into, inspiration: divinus.

inflexus2.definition: īnflexus ūs, m 1 in+FALC-, a bending, curving: vicorum, Iu.

infra1.definition: īnfrā adv. for inferā, sc. parte, on the under side, below, underneath: infra nihil est nisi mortale: partes eae, quae sunt infra quam id quod devoratur: infra Quam solet esse, O.: exemplum infra scriptum est, S.: one…

infra2.definition: īnfrā praep. with acc. 1 infra, below, under, beneath: infra oppidum: infra caelum nox cadit, Ta.—Of time, later than: Homerus non infra superiorem Lycurgum fuit.—Of size, smaller than: magnitudine paulo infra elephan…

infrenatus1.definition: īn-frēnātus adj., without a bridle: equites infrenati, on unbridled horses, L.

infrendo.definition: (īn-frendō, —, —, ere) to gnash.—Only P. praes.: dentibus infrendens gemitu, V.

infrenis.definition: īnfrēnis —, adj. 2 in+frenum, without a bridle, unbridled: equus, V.

infrons.definition: īnfrōns ondis, adj. 2 in+frons, without foliage, destitute of trees: agri, O.

ingeniose.definition: ingeniōsē adv. ingeniosus, acutely, wittily, ingeniously: nihil (excogitat): electas res conlocare, Iu.

ingenue.definition: ingenuē adv. ingenuus, as becomes his birth, liberally, frankly: educatus: confiteri.

ingigno.definition: (in-gīgnō) genuī, genitus, ere, to implant, engender: cupiditatem homini: animantibus conservandi sui custodiam.

ingrate.definition: ingrātē adv. ingratus, unpleasantly: Sunt quibus ingrate indulgentia servit, O.—Unthankfully, ungratefully: necessitudinis nomen repudiare.

ingratiis.definition: in-grātiīs (T., C.) or in-grātīs (C., N.), adv., without thanks, unwillingly, involuntarily, on compulsion: coacta ingratiis, T.: ingratiis ut dormiam, T.: nisi plane cogit ingratiis: dicent quae necesse erit, ingrati…

ingressus2.definition: ingressus ūs, m 1 in+GRAD-, an advancing, walking, gait: ingressus, cursus, accubitio: prohiberi ingressu, could not stir, Cs.: instabilis, L.— Fig.: ingressūs capere, begins, V.—A going in, entering: in forum: ingres…

inguen.definition: inguen inis, n ANG-, the groin: destillat ab inguine virus, V.: candida succincta inguina (Scylla), V.: ventrem atque inguina hausit, L.—A swelling, tumor.— The privy parts, H., O., Iu.

inhoneste.definition: inhonestē adv. inhonestus, dishonorably, disgracefully: parere divitias, T.: accusare.

inhonoratus.definition: in-honōrātus adj. with comp. and sup, unhonored, disregarded: vita: inhonoratior triumphus, L.: dea, O.—Without reward, unrewarded: regem inhonoratum dimittere, L.: gentium inhonoratissimi post victoriam, L.: nos, O.

inhumane.definition: inhūmānē adv. with comp. inhumanus, cruelly, inhumanly: cruciat adulescentulum, T.: inhumanius dicere.

inhumaniter.definition: inhūmāniter adv. inhumanus, uncivilly, discourteously: fecisse: respondit.

inhumatus.definition: in-humātus unburied: nec inhumati nec deserti: Coniunx, V.

iniectus2.definition: (iniectus) ūs, m inicio, a casting on, throwing over.—Only abl: multae vestis, Ta.

inimice.definition: inimīcē adv. with comp. and sup. inimicus, as an enemy, inimically: tecum agere: insectari: inimicius consulere, L.: inimicissime contendere.

inique.definition: inīquē adv. with comp. and sup. iniquus, unequally: Quam inique comparatum est, T.: iniquius Certatio comparata, more unequally matched, T.: iniquissime comparatum est.—Fig., unfairly, unjustly: damnati: occidere, L.:…

initus2.definition: initus ūs, m 1 in+1 I-, an entrance, O.

iniucunde.definition: (iniūcundē) adv. iniucundus, unpleasantly. —Only comp: res iniucundius actae.

iniucunditas.definition: iniūcunditās ātis, f iniucundus, unpleasantness: ne quid habeat iniucunditatis oratio.

iniucundus.definition: in-iūcundus adj., unpleasant, disagreeable: minime nobis labor: adversus malos, harsh, Ta.

iniungo.definition: in-iungō ūnxī, ūnctus, ere, to join, fasten, attach: tignos in asseres, L.: vineas moenibus.— Fig., to inflict, impose, enjoin, occasion, bring upon: civitatibus servitutem, Cs.: privatis onus, L.: iniuriam a nobis re…

iniuratus.definition: in-iūrātus adj., unsworn, not under oath: cum dicit iniuratus: iurati iniuratique fugiunt, L.

iniuria.definition: iniūria ae, f iniurius, an injustice, wrong, outrage, injury, insult: (filius) carens patriā ob meas iniurias, harsh treatment, T.: paterna, T.: iniuriam sibi imponere: privatas iniurias ultus est, Cs.: in populum R.,…

iniuriose.definition: iniūriōsē adv. with comp. iniuriosus, unjustly, unlawfully: in alqo decernere: tractati.

iniuriosus.definition: iniūriōsus adj. iniuria, unjust, wrongful, harmful: in proximos: ab invito emere iniuriosum esse: pes, H.

iniurius.definition: iniūrius adj. 2 in+ius, unlawful, injurious, wrongful, unjust: sibi esse iniurius videri, T.: Id possum ferre quamquam iniuriumst, T.: quia sit iniurium: indictā causā damnari absentem iniurium esse, L.

iniussus1.definition: in-iūssus adj., unbidden, voluntary, of one's own accord: cantare Iniussi numquam desistant, H.: iniussae veniunt ad mulctra capellae, H.: iniussa virescunt Gramina, spontaneous, V.—Plur n. as subst: Non iniussa cano,…

iniussus2.definition: (in-iūssus, ūs) m without command.—Only abl: iniussu suo et civitatis, Cs.: iniussu praetoris: signa referunt, without orders, L.

iniuste.definition: iniūstē adv. with sup. iniustus, without right, unjustly: facere: totum ducit poema, H.: iniustissime, S.

iniustitia.definition: iniūstitia ae, f iniustus, injustice, unfairness: iniustitiae duo genera sunt.—Severity, harshness: Eum ego hinc eieci iniustitiā meā , T.

iniustus.definition: in-iūstus adj. with comp. and sup, unreasonable, unsuitable, oppressive, excessive, improper, severe, burdensome: iusta iniusta omnia obsequi, humor you in everything, T.: onus: fascis, V.: supplicia, S.: faenus, L.—U…

inlabefactus.definition: 'in-labefactus (ill-) adj., unbroken, uninterrupted: adfinia vincula, O.: concordia, O.'

inlabor.definition: in-lābor (ill-) lapsus, ī, dep., to flow in, glide in, fall, sink: Si fractus inlabatur orbis, fall to ruins, H.: quo (in stomachum) primo inlabuntur ea, etc.: mediae urbi, V.—Fig., to flow in, penetrate: ad eos (sens…

inlaboro.definition: in-labōrō (ill-) —, —, āre, to work upon, work at: domibus (i. e. aedificandis), Ta.

inlacessitus.definition: in-lacessītus (ill-) adj., unprovoked, unattacked: pacem inlacessiti nutrierunt, Ta.: Britanniae pars, undisturbed, Ta.

inlacrimabilis.definition: in-lacrimābilis (ill-) e, adj., unwept, unlamented: omnes inlacrimabiles Urgentur Nocte, H. —Not moved by tears, pitiless: Pluto, H.

inlacrimo.definition: inlacrimō (ill-) āvī, ātus, āre 1 in+lacrima, dep., to weep over, sorrow for, bewail, lament: qui dicitur inlacrimans dixisse: Sic ait inlacrimans, V.: gaudio, L.: inlacrima patris pestibus: casu, N.: maestum inlacrim…

inlacrimor.definition: inlacrimor ātus, ārī, dep. 1 in+lacrima, to weep over, lament: inlacrimare, H.: cuius morti.

inlaesus.definition: 'in-laesus (ill-) adj., unhurt, unharmed, unmutilated: inlaeso corpore, O.: partes, O.'

inlaetabilis.definition: in-laetābilis (ill-) e, adj., cheerless, joyless, gloomy, sad: ora, V.: murmur, V.

inlaqueo.definition: in-laqueō (ill-) —, ātus, āre 1 in+laqueus, to ensnare, entrap, entangle: munera navium inlaqueant duces, H.: inlaqueatus legum periculis.

inlaudatus.definition: in-laudātus (ill-) adj., unpraised, infamous: Busiris, V.

inlecebra.definition: 'inlecebra (ill-) ae, f 1 in+1 LAC-, an enticement, inducement, attraction, charm, allurement, bait, lure: ad quam inlecebram cum commoveretur nemo, etc., L.: suis te oportet inlecebris virtus trahat: inlecebris erat …

inlepide.definition: inlepidē (ill-) adv. inlepidus, impolitely, rudely, inelegantly: (poema) Compositum, H.

inlepidus.definition: 'in-lepidus (ill-) adj., unmannerly, rude, disagreeable: parens, Caecil. ap. C.: deliciae, Ct.'

inlibatus.definition: in-lībātus (ill-) adj., undiminished, unimpaired: divitiae: vires, L.: imperium, L.

inliberalis.definition: in-līberālis (ill-) e, adj., ignoble, ungenerous, vulgar, sordid, mean, disobliging: quaestūs: facinus, T.: iocandi genus: Servos, T.: in me, disobliging.—Niggardly, petty: adiectio, L.

inliberalitas.definition: inlīberālitās (ill-) ātis, f inliberalis, meanness, stinginess: inliberalitatis suspicio.

inliberaliter.definition: inlīberāliter (ill-) adv. inliberalis, ignobly, ungenerously, meanly: factum a vobis, T.: aestimare, i. e. stingily.

inlicio.definition: inliciō (ill-) lexī, lectus, ere (inlēxe for inlēxisse, Att. ap. C.) 1 in+lacio, to allure, entice, attract, seduce, inveigle, decoy: coniugem in stuprum: Imperitos rerum in fraudem, T.: inlecti <*>d proditionem, S.: …

inlicitator.definition: inlicitātor (ill-) ōris, m * inlicitor, a shambidder, bidder-in, mock-purchaser: non inlicitatorem apponet: ponere.

inlicitus.definition: 'in-licitus (ill-) adj., not allowed, unlawful, illicit: amor, Ta.: exactiones, Ta.'

inlido.definition: inlīdō (ill-) sī, sus, ere 1 in+laedo, to dash against, push against: caestūs effracto in ossa cerebro, V.: ad volnus manūs: pila vadis inlisa, V.: repagula ossibus, O.: dentem fragili (corpori), H.—To crush: serpens …

inligo.definition: in-ligō (ill-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bind on, tie on, fasten, attach: tauris iuga, H.: inligata tigna tenere, Cs.: manibus post tergum inligatis, L.: emblemata in poculis: litterae in iaculo inligatae, Cs.: lunae motūs i…

inlimis.definition: inlīmis (ill-) e, adj. 2 in+limus, without mud: fons, i. e. clear, O.

inlino.definition: in-linō (ill-) lēvī, litus, ere, to smear over, spread upon, lay on: oculis collyria, H.: nivīs agris, spreads, H.: alqd chartis, has written, H.— To besmear, bedaub, anoint: malleolos stuppae pice, L.: texta Nesseo v…

inlitteratus.definition: inlitterātus (ill-) adj., unlettered, unlearned, without culture, inelegant: multi: in sermone multa: nervi, H.

inlotus.definition: in-lōtus (ill-), or in-lautus adj., unwashed, unclean, dirty: toralia, H.—Not washed away: sudor, V.

inlucesco.definition: in-lūcēscō (ill-) lūxī, —, ere, inch, to grow light, begin to shine, break, dawn: Inlucescet aliquando ille dies, cum, etc.: cum tertio die sol inluxisset: alios Inluxisse dies, V.—Perf impers., it was light, day had …

inludo.definition: in-lūdō (ill-) sī (inlūsseris, C.), sus, ere, to play at, sport with: haec Inludo chartis, sportively throw on paper, H.: Inlusae auro vestes, gayly inwrought, V. (al. inclusae).—To make sport, make game of, mock, jee…

inlumino.definition: in-lūminō (ill-) āvī, ātus, āre, to light up, make light, illuminate: luna inluminata a sole.— Fig., in rhet., to set off, illustrate: tamquam stellis orationem: illuminata sapientia.

inlusio.definition: inlūsiō (ill-) ōnis, f LVD-, a mocking, jeering.

inlustre.definition: (inlūstrē) adv. inlustris, clearly, manifestly. —Only comp: inlustrius (vidi me amari).

inlustris.definition: inlūstris (ill-) e, adj. with comp. LVC-, lighted, bright, light, lustrous, brilliant: domicilia: caput, O.: solis candor inlustrior est quam ullius ignis.—Fig., clear, plain, distinct, evident, manifest: ad cognoscen…

invidiose.definition: invidiōsē adv. invidiosus, enviously, hatefully: criminari.

inviolate.definition: inviolātē adv. inviolatus, inviolably: memoriam nostri servare.

inviolatus.definition: in-violātus adj., unhurt, inviolate: involnerati inviolatique: amicitia: Visam inviolatus amnem, H.: fama, without reproach, S.—Inviolable: legati, nomen ad omnīs inviolatum: templum, L.: fides publica, S.

invisus1.definition: invīsus adj. with comp. P. of invideo, hated, hateful, detested: persona: alios invisos efficere, L.: penates, O.: (Helena) aris invisa sedebat, V.: invisos nos esse illis, T.: omnibus, S.: hominibus invisius animal: …

invisus2.definition: in-vīsus adj., unseen: res, Cs.: sacra maribus invisa.

invitatus.definition: (invītātus, ūs) m invito, an inviting, invitation.— Only abl: invitatu tuo.

invite.definition: (īnvītē) adv. with comp, against one's will, unwillingly: cepi Capuam: invitius accedere.

invocatus2.definition: in-vocātus adj., uncalled, without a summons: ad dormientem veniunt (imagines) invocatae.—Uninvited, without an invitation: ut mihi . . . invocato sit locus, T.: ut quos invocatos vidisset in foro, omnes devocaret, N.

involatus.definition: (involātus, ūs) m a flying, flight; only abl: ex alitis involatu auguror.

involutus.definition: involūtus adj. P. of involvo, involved, intricate, obscure: res.

iocatio.definition: iocātiō ōnis, f iocor, a joking, joke, jest.

iocor.definition: iocor ātus, ārī, dep. iocus, to jest, joke: tu hanc iocari credis? T.: duplex iocandi genus: voluit Fortuna iocari, Iu.—To say in jest: haec: in faciem permulta, H.: nescio quid, Ct.

iocose.definition: iocōsē adv. with comp, jestingly, jocosely: eumque lusi iocose satis: iocosius scribere.

iocosus.definition: iocōsus adj. iocus, full of jesting, jocose, humorous, droll, facetious, sportive: Maecenas, H.: Musa, O.: res: verba, O.: furtum, H.: Nilus (i. e. of the merry Egyptians), O.

iocularis.definition: ioculāris e, adj. ioculus, facetious, jocular, laughable, droll: audacia, T.—Plur n. as subst, jests, jokes, H.

iocularius.definition: ioculārius adj. ioculus, ludicrous, droll: malum, T.

ioculator.definition: ioculātor ōris, m ioculor, a jester, joker: senex.

ioculor.definition: (ioculor) —, ārī ioculus, to jest, joke; only P. praes.: quaedam militariter ioculantes, L.

iocus.definition: iocus ī (plur. also ioca, iocorum, n), m IA-, a jest, joke: iocum movere, S.: ioci causā, for the sake of the joke: ioca atque seria cum humillimis agere, S.: seria ac iocos celebrare, L.: conviva ioco mordente facetu…

iracunde.definition: īrācundē adv. with comp. iracundus, angrily, passionately: agere cum aliquo: iracundius expostulare.

iratus.definition: īrātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of irascor, angered, enraged, angry, violent, furious: animus, T.: nihil feci iratus, in anger: quid irati sentire possunt? in their wrath, Cs.: tibi graviter, T.: adversario iudex: …

isti.definition: istī old for 2 istic, there, V. (Ribb.).

istic1.definition: istic aec, oc and uc (with -ne, istucine), pron demonstr. iste+ce.— Referring to that which is at hand or related to the person addressed, that of yours, that mentioned by you: istaec res, T.: circum istaec loca commo…

istic2.definition: istīc adv., there, in that place, where you are: quid istic tibi negotist? T.: quoniam istic sedes: quocumque istic loco constitisti, L.—Herein, in this affair, on this occasion: Neque istic, neque alibi, T.: Istic su…

isto.definition: istō adv. iste, thither, to you, to where you are: si minima causa est properandi isto mihi.— Thereinto, in that matter: Trabatium isto admiscere.

istuc.definition: istūc adv. istic, thither, to you, to where you are, in that direction: Concede istuc paululum, T.: istuc sunt delapsi: istuc mens animusque Fert, H.— To that thing, to that subject: istuc ibam, T.

ita.definition: ita adv. 2 I-. I. In gen., referring to what precedes, in this manner, in this wise, in such a way, so, thus, accordingly, as has been said: des operam ut investiges sitne ita: Ita aiunt, T.: his rebus ita actis, S.: …

itaque.definition: ita-que conj, and so, and thus, and accordingly: Si cetera ita sunt ut vis, itaque ut esse ego illa existumo, T.: ita constitui, itaque feci.—In inference, and so, accordingly, therefore, for that reason, consequently…

item.definition: item adv., likewise, besides, also, further, moreover, too, as well: Unus et item alter, T.: Lentulus, itemque ceteri, S.: Romulus augur cum fratre item augure: Contemplator item, cum, etc., V.— In the phrase, non ite…

iuba.definition: iuba ae, f DIV-, a mane, flowing hair on the neck: equus ille iubam quatiens, C. poët.: iubae equorum, Cs.: luduntque iubae, etc., V.: equinae, O.— A crest: triplici crinita iubā galea, V.: iubas Divini adsimulat capi…

iubar.definition: iubar arīs, n DIV-, radiance, light, splendor, brightness, sunshine: iubare exorto, V.: Quintus nitidum iubar extulit Lucifer, O.: Hanc animam, Fac iubar, i. e. make into a constellation, O.

iubatus.definition: iubātus adj. iuba, crested: anguis, L.

iucunde.definition: iūcundē (iōc-) adv. with comp. and sup. iucundus, agreeably, delightfully: vivere: cenam producere, H.: bibere iucundius: iucundissime vivere.

iucunditas.definition: iūcunditās (iōc-) ātis, f iucundus, agreeableness, pleasantness, delight, enjoyment: agri: epistula plena iucunditatis: dare se iucunditati, to enjoyment: ea est in homine iucunditas, ut, cheerfulness: plurimae tuae i…

iucundus.definition: iūcundus (iōc-) adj. with comp. and sup. DIV-, pleasant, agreeable, delightful, pleasing: est mihi iucunda vestra erga me voluntas: id vero militibus fuit iucundum, Cs.: praemia, H.: Crispi iucunda senectus (i. e. sen…

iudex.definition: iūdex icis, m and f ius+DIC-, a judge, juror: verissimus: nequam et levis: severissimi atque integerrimi: te ipsum habebo iudicem: quem si ferrem iudicem, proposed: ferre Volscio iudicem, L.: iudicem dicere, i. e. sub…

iudicatio.definition: iūdicātiō ōnis, f iudico, a judging, investigating: Longi subselli.—A judicial examination: Iudicatio est, etc.—Fig., a judgment, opinion: iudicatio se scire quod nesciat.

iudicatum.definition: iūdicātum ī, n P. n. of iudico, a decision, judgment, decree: iudicatum facere, to carry out. —An award, fine: solvere.

iudicatus1.definition: iūdicātus adj. P. of iudico, decided, determined: res iudicata, a precedent: infirmatio rerum iudicatarum.—As subst, a condemned person: iudicatum duci.

iudicatus2.definition: iūdicātus ūs, m iudico, a judgeship, office of judge: isti ordini iudicatus non patebit.

iudicialis.definition: iūdiciālis e, adj. iudicium, of a court of justice, judicial: ius: tabella: genus (dicendi), juridical pleading.

iudiciarius.definition: iūdiciārius adj. iudicium, of the courts, judiciary: lex: quaestus: controversia.

iudicium.definition: iūdicium ī, n iudex, a judgment, judicial investigation, trial, legal process, sentence: omnia iudicia reperta sunt, etc.: dignitatis meae, concerning: de meā fide: inter sicarios, for assassination: vocare in iudiciu…

iugalis.definition: iugālis e, adj. iugum, of a yoke, yoked together: equi iumentaque, Cu.—Plur m. as subst, a team: gemini, V.—Matrimonial, nuptial: ne cui me vinclo sociare iugali, V.: dona, O.

iugatio.definition: iugātiō ōnis, f iugo, a binding.

iugatus.definition: iugātus adj. P. of iugo, connected, dependent: virtutes inter se: verba, kindred.

iugerum.definition: iūgerum ī, n gen plur. iūgerūm; dat. and abl. iū geribus, n IV-, an acre, juger (containing 28,000 square feet): decumanum: quaterna in singulos iugera, Cs.: nescio quotenorum iugerum: per tota novem iugera Porrigitur…

iugis1.definition: iūgis e, adj. IV-, joined together: auspicium, i. e. of a yoke of oxen.

iugis2.definition: iūgis e, adj. VIV-, fresh, living, perennial: putei: aqua, S., H.

iuglans.definition: iūglāns glandis, f Iovis+glans, a walnut, walnut-tree: iuglandium putamina.

iugo.definition: iugō āvī, ātus, āre iugum, to bind, marry: alcui intactam, V.: decreta super iugandis Feminis, H.

iugosus.definition: iugōsus adj. iugum, mountainous: silvae, O.

iugulo.definition: iugulō āvī, ātus, āre iugulum, to cut the throat, kill, slay, murder: finis iugulandi, S.: civīs iugulari iussit: homines, H.: tum rite sacratas In flammam iugulant pecudes, slaughter and throw, V.— Fig., to destroy, …

iugulum.definition: iugulum ī, n (iugulus, ī, m, Iu.), dim. iugum, the collar-bone, hollow part of the neck: iugula concava habere.—The throat, neck: mucrones a iugulis vestris deiecimus: recludere stricto ense, O.: iugulos aperire susur…

iugum.definition: iugum ī, n IV-, a yoke, collar: in iugo insistere, Cs.: bestiis iuga imponimus: (bos) iuga detractans, V.: iuga demere Bobus, H.—A yoke, pair, team: ut minus multis iugis ararent: inmissa iuga, pair of horses, V.: cur…

iumentum.definition: iūmentum ī, n IV-, a beast for hauling, draught-animal, beast of burden, horse, mule, ass: iumenta onerat, S.: iumento nihil opus est (i. e. equo): sarcinaria, beasts of burden, Cs.: servi ut taceant, iumenta loquentu…

iunceus.definition: iunceus adj. iuncus, made of rushes: vincula, O.—Fig., slim, slender: alquam reddunt iunceam, T.

iuncosus.definition: iuncōsus adj. iuncus, full of rushes: litora, O.

iunctio.definition: iūnctiō ōnis, f IV-, a joining, uniting.

iunctura.definition: iūnctūra ae, f IV-, a joining, uniting, juncture, joint: tignorum, Cs.: iuncturae verticis, sutures, O.: laterum iuncturas fibula mordet, the united ends of the girdle, V.—Fig., a connection: generis, i. e. consanguin…

iunctus.definition: iūnctus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of iungo, united, connected, associated, kindred: iunctis Frontibus, in a line, V.: Per dies et iunctas noctīs, following, O.: causa cum exitu iunctior: iunctissimus illi comes, mos…

iuncus.definition: iuncus ī, m a rush: Limosus, V.: acutā cuspide iunci, O.

iungo.definition: iungō ūnxī, ūnctus, ere IV-, to join together, unite, connect, attach, fasten, yoke, harness: Narcissum et florem anethi, V.: ostia, shut, Iu.: iunctas quatere fenestras, H.: oscula, exchange, O.: da iungere dextram, …

iuniperus.definition: iūniperus ī, f the juniper-tree, V.

iurator.definition: iūrātor ōris, m iuro, a swearer, assistant of the censor, sworn census-clerk, L.

iuratus.definition: iūrātus adj. P. of iuror, sworn, under oath, bound by an oath: qui iuratus apud vos dixit: homines, jurors: testis, Iu.: in eadem arma, O.— As subst m.: huius iurati testimonium, witness.— As subst n.: iurata, solemn …

iurgium.definition: iūrgium ī, n ius+1 AG-, a quarrel, strife, dispute, altercation, contention: inde ad iurgium, T.: iurgiis trahendo tempus, S.: benevolorum concertatio iurgium dicitur: iurgia iactare, quarrel, V.: vicina refugere iurg…

iurgo.definition: iūrgō āvī, ātus, āre * iūrigus; IV-, to quarrel, brawl, dispute, scold: Cedo, quid iurgabit tecum? T.: iurgare vicinos, non litigare: haec iurgans agebat, with expostulation, L.: istis Iurgatur verbis, is reproached, H.

iuridicialis.definition: iūridiciālis e, adj. iuridicus, relating to right, of justice: genus: quaestio.

iuris1.definition: iūris cōnsultus a lawyer; see consultus.

iuris3.definition: iūris perītus learned in the law; see peritus.

iuro.definition: iūrō āvī, ātus, āre 2 ius, to swear, take an oath: si aram tenens iuraret: ex animi tui sententiā, without reservation: Boeotum in crasso iurares aëre natum, H.: falsum, swear falsely: vere: testari deos per quos iura…

iuror.definition: (iūror ātus, ārī,) dep., see iuro and iuratus.

ius1.definition: iūs iūris, n IV-, broth, soup, sauce: hesternum, T.: fervens: tepidum, H.—In a pun: Verrinum, hog-broth (the justice of Verres).

ius2.definition: iūs iūris (dat. iūre, L.; plur. only nom. and acc.), n IV-, that which is binding, right, justice, duty: ius hominum situm est in societate, etc.: obtinere, maintain: de iure alicui respondere, lay down the law: clien…

iussum.definition: iūssum ī, n P. neut. of iubeo, an order, command, ordinance, law: deorum immortalium iussa: iussis vostris oboediens, S.: horrida iussa, V.: iussis carmina coepta tuis, V.: efficere, execute, S.: capessere, accept, V.…

iussus2.definition: (iūssus, ūs) m an order, command, decree, ordinance (only abl sing.): vestro iussu coactus: lecti iussu populi, L.: sine populi iussu, S.: dei, V.: Neronis, Iu.

iuste.definition: iūstē adv. with comp. and sup. iustus, rightly, justly, equitably, duly: accusare: Ambo miseri, sed iustius illa, with better cause, O.: ornare hunc iustissime.

iustificus.definition: iūstificus adj. iustus+2 FAC-, that acts justly: mens deorum, Ct.

iustitia.definition: iūstitia ae, f iustus, justice, equity, righteousness, uprightness: labore atque iustitiā res p. crevit, S.: summa hominis: erga deos.— Person., V.: potens, H.—Clemency, compassion: pro eius iustitiā impetrare, Cs.: t…

iustitium.definition: iūstitium n 2 ius+STA-, a suspension of the courts, judicial vacation, holiday: iustitium edici oportere: quadriduum, L.: iustitium remittitur, L.— A public mourning, Ta.

iustus.definition: iūstus adj. with comp. and sup. 2 ius, just, upright, righteous: iudex: in socios: qui omnium iustissimus fuisse traditur.—In accordance with law, right, equitable, just: lex: supplicia: bella, O.: iustissimos triumph…

iuvenalis.definition: iuvenālis e, adj. iuvenis, youthful, juvenile, suitable for young people: amor, V.: ludus, L.: anni, O.—Plur n. as subst, youthful games, Ta.

iuvenaliter.definition: iuvenāliter adv. iuvenalis, in a youthful manner, youthfully: Iecit aurum, O.—Rashly, improvidently, O.

iuvenca.definition: iuvenca ae, f iuvencus, a young cow, heifer: formosa, V.: votiva, H.— A girl: Graia, i. e. Helen, O.: tua, H.

iuvencus.definition: iuvencus ī, m iuvenis, a young bullock: aratra iugo referunt suspensa iuvenci, V.: fessi iuvenci, O.: Te suis matres metuunt iuvencis young men, H.

iuvenesco.definition: iuvenēscō —, —, ere, inch. iuvenis, to attain youth, grow up: vitulus . . . largis iuvenescit herbis, H.—To grow young, regain youth: Pylius iuvenescere posset, O.

iuvenilis.definition: iuvenīlis e, adj. with comp. iuvenis, of youth, youthful, juvenile: dicendi impunitas: membra, Iu.: suis semper iuvenilior annis, O.: sidus iuvenile nepotes, a youthful constellation, O. —Plur n. as subst: iuvenilia l…

iuveniliter.definition: iuvenīliter adv. iuvenilis, after the manner of youth: exsultare.

iuvenor.definition: iuvenor —, —, ārī, dep. iuvenis, to act with youthful indiscretion, wanton: teneris versibus, H.

iuventa.definition: iuventa ae, f iuvenis, the age of youth, youth: membra decora iuventā , V.: primā a parte iuventae: ita se a iuventā gessisse, L.: citra iuventam, in boyhood, O.—Youth, young folk: docilis, H.—Person., the goddess of …

iuventas.definition: iuventās ātis, f iuvenis, the age of youth, youth, V.; of the eagle, youthful vigor, H.—Person., youth, the goddess of youth, C.: comis, H.

iuventus.definition: iuventūs ūtis, f iuvenis, the age of youth, youth (from twenty to forty): quae iuventute geruntur et viribus: iuventutem suam exercuit, S. — Young persons, youth: pleraque, S.: omnis: Troiana, V.: Alcinoi, i. e. Phaea…

iuvo.definition: iuvō iūvī, iūtus (iuvātūrus, S.), āre DIV-, to help, aid, assist, further, serve, support, benefit: aut consilio aut re, T.: non multum ad summam victoriae, Cs.: alquem commeatu: domum atque liberos, H.: te portuque l…

iuxta1.definition: iūxtā adv. for * iūgistā, abl f. sup. from iūgis, near to, nigh, near at hand, near, near by, hard by, close to, by the side of: legio, quae iuxta constiterat, Cs.: sellam iuxta ponere, S.: furiarum maxima iuxta Accub…

iuxta2.definition: iūxtā praep. with acc. 1 iuxta, very near, close to, near to, hard by: iuxta eum castra posuit, Cs.: iuxta focum agunt, Ta.: hanc (aram) iuxta, N.: vicina Ceraunia iuxta, V.—Next to, immediately after, beside, on a pa…
